claims.claim_vi: In the bank example, Bob opens an account and deposits $100 in cash at Bank of America (the cash goes to the vault, the wallet system creates account B1234); using Citibank means repeating the process.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: A bank transfer deducts from the sender's account and credits the receiver's at once, but the cash only moves when the two banks settle all transactions at end of day.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: On a blockchain there is no cash: the user generates an address, keeps the private key in a crypto wallet such as Metamask, and signs a transaction to send (Bob sends 2 ether to Alice's address; once confirmed Bob has 8 ether and Alice 101 ether).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit. The source does not state the starting balances; 10 and 99 follow from the amounts it gives.

claims.claim_vi: The source says a blockchain is a distributed ledger offering one interface for common wallet operations, confirms transfers in pseudo real time, and can merge wallet services of different banks into one global service.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Fees, the time a confirmation takes and the loss of a private key are not in the source; the lesson mentions them as general knowledge only.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against a blockchain's documentation.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung cùng ba bước (gửi/nhận, chuyển, rút/xác nhận) đặt cạnh nhau, rồi một khung ghi ba điểm khác. Không có mũi tên giữa hai khung vì chúng là hai cách làm, không phải hai bước nối nhau.
source_deviations: Source ends with "Can you spot the differences?"; the lesson answers it in a notes section and in the question at the end.
The source says transfers are confirmed in pseudo real time; the lesson adds, as general knowledge, that confirmation still takes time and fees exist, and marks that as unchecked.
The source says blockchains can merge wallet services into one global service; the lesson presents that as the source's claim, not as an established fact.
